headline: Deep models link omics layers to gene regulation, imaging, and clinical outcomes
label: Deep Learning Omics Prediction
summary: Recent items test learned models on transfer from bulk to single-cell data, imaging-genomics links, and pediatric outcome prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a learned model judged against explicit benchmarks or transfer tests rather than fit alone. scOPE carries frozen driver-associated expression axes learned in bulk tumours onto single-cell transcriptomes and attaches a ground-truth-free confidence score, while CSOA is benchmarked against sixteen single-cell gene set enrichment methods. DirectRanker is benchmarked against random forest and logistic regression for threshold-free expression ranking from five histone marks, and clinTALL performs competing-risk outcome prediction in pediatric T-ALL. Evo 2 variant severity scores, correlated with TCGA tumor radiomics, yield gene-imaging associations including 46 new renal cancer genes. What is new is the coupling of foundation-model or deep architectures to cross-scale transfer: bulk to single cell, sequence to imaging, histone marks to expression rank. The set is methodologically heterogeneous, so this describes a dominant pattern rather than a shared one.
